the_finding: The acceptance names TWELVE opcodes. Measured against this campaign's own evidence, 2 are live and bound (DENSE_Q, RECURRENT_BLOCK), one is measured but unbound (TERNARY_PLANES), one is real only for a fixed distribution (LATENT_TRANSFORM), and the remaining EIGHT are refuted, unbuilt, vacuous or inapplicable. An ISA frozen as specified would be two-thirds dead surface, and every dead opcode is a runtime branch that must be maintained, verified and trusted forever.

shared_vm_vs_marginal_model_bytes.note: The verify says shared VM bytes must be reported separately and never omitted. They are 6.27 MB of runtime against 14.30 GB of artifact -- 0.044%. The sharing argument for a pooled VM is therefore not a BYTES argument on this machine; it would have to be a correctness or maintenance argument.

the_independent_verifier_has_a_measured_: The verify's premise is that Gravity can produce false wins. This session alone caught SEVEN method defects that would have shipped as findings: a max-curvature rule degenerate on a 3-point grid (G067), a budget sweep that made its answer uniform by construction (G073), a LANGUAGE answer key that marked the REFERENCE model wrong (G076), a 48-token budget that scored every artifact 0.00 (G076), a control compared at unequal cost (G081), an amortized column that printed the serial number twice (G091), and a finding generalised from one capture site to all five (F10). Every one was a MEASUREMENT defect, not an artifact defect. So an independent verifier that checks only reproducible builds and content-addressed inputs would have caught NONE of them -- it must verify the measurement method, not just the bytes.
